en: Title: Sumukhā Dhāraṇī Sources: Five Sanskrit fragments (Bongard-Levin et al.; Emmerick);
Tibetan: D 614/915.
Bongard-Levin, G.M., M.I.
Vorobyeva-Desyatovskaya, and E.N. Tyomkin. “A Fragment of the Sanskrit *Sumukhadhāraṇī*. *Indo-Iranian Journal* 10, no. 2/3 (1967): 150–53, 155–59.

*Husavati puṣavati hili hili, as fearless as fire, as fearless as the supreme, as fearless as the thunderbolt, as fearless as the heart!* This *dhāraṇī*, named "The Auspicious Face of Vajrapāṇi," was spoken by the Tathāgata for the benefit of all sentient beings out of compassion; I too shall speak it, just as it was spoken and empowered by those former Perfectly Awakened Ones, and established by him who is true to his vow. Then, from the mark of a great man on the Bhagavat’s chest, a ray of light was emitted. An illumination appeared throughout all Buddha-fields, and the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, being impelled by that ray of light, set out from their respective Buddha-fields toward the Sahā Buddha-field.
(2) Bongard-Levin, G.M. ‘A New Fragment of the Sanskrit *Sumukhadhāraṇī* and Its Saka Version’. *Indologica Taurinensia* 8–9, no. 1 (1980): 45–49.

"Furthermore, Venerable Blessed One, I shall provide protection for that son of good family or daughter of good family, as follows: *tadyathā hihi vajra hihi vajra hihi vajra* ... *kiri kiri vajra svāhā*. *Tadyathā aṇḍare paṇḍare śvete pāṇḍaravāsini kinnare karāḍe keyūre iha buddha buddhe tatra buddhe bhūje jaṃgame bhūjapani bhayaṃ bhaye bhayāgre bhayāgrapate vinī vinī śīramapathe ādityapathe teje tejapathe akārapathe ākārapathe phu svāhā.* Then the great rākṣasī Vajrabhūti (Vajradūtī) bowed with palms joined toward the Blessed One and said this to the Blessed One: 'I too, Venerable Blessed One, shall provide protection for that son of good family, as follows: *tadyathā kuṭse kuṭse kuṭsa vikuṭsare svāhā*. *Nīle nīlakeśe svāhā*. *Nīle nīle keśe svāhā*. *Pītakeśe svāhā*. *Lohite lohi...*"

(3) Bongard-Levin, G.M. ‘A New Fragment of the Sanskrit Sumukhadhāraṇī’. In *Tibetan and Buddhist Studies: Commemorating the 200th Anniversary of the Birth of Alexander Csoma de Kőrös*, vol. 1, edited by Louis Ligeti. *Bibliotheca Orientalis Hungarica*, XXIX/1. Budapest: Akadémiai Kiadó, 1984, pp. 125–129.

—*Je kaṭe kaṭu kaṃmale* (variant: *kambale*) *brahme brahmasvare brahmasiddhe siddhamanorathe phu svāhā*. The Great Goddess Vajraśaṅkalā (variant: Vajraśṛṅkhalā) addressed the Blessed One: “Blessed One, I too shall speak these dhāraṇī words for the sake of protecting and guarding that son of good family or daughter of good family who shall uphold this Dharma discourse of Sumukha, and who, having risen at dawn, shall recite it: *Tadyathā*: *Vajre vajre vajre mahāvajre vajramate buddhavajre buddhādhiṣṭhitavajre ubuddhe nibuddhe saṃbuddhe bahubuddhe viśiṣṭabuddhe buddhe buddhe buddhe buddhe buddhe diśaṃgame jaṃgame aleme tilome tile tile tilele mārge mārgantagāmini svāhā*. Then the Bodhisattva Vajrasena addressed the Blessed One: “Blessed One, I too shall provide protection for that son of good family or daughter of good family who shall uphold this Dharma discourse of Sumukha, this vidyā-mantra for the preservation of life, and who, having risen at dawn, shall recite it: *Tadyathā*: *Hihi vajre*...”

(4) Bongard-Levin, G.M., and M.I. Vorobyeva-Desyatovskaya. “Novyi Tekst Fragmenta Sanskritskoi ‘Sumukkha-Dhāraṇī’ [A New Text from the Fragment of the Sanskrit *Sumukha-Dhāraṇī*]. *Peredneaziatskii Sbornik* [Western Asian Almanac] (Moscow) 4 (1986): 156–59.

As it was in the heart [of the Buddhas]: "O Vajrapāṇi, this is that dhāraṇī named Sumukhā, spoken by all the Tathāgatas for the benefit of sentient beings out of compassion; I too shall speak it, just as it was spoken and empowered by those former Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones, established through their vow of truth. Then, from the *ūrṇā* hair-treasure, the mark of a Great Man, a ray of light was emitted by the Blessed One, and by it an illumination appeared in all the Buddha-fields, and by that very [light]...
(5) Emmerick, Ronald Eric. “Another Fragment of the Sanskrit Sumukhadhāraṇī. In *Deyadharma: Studies in Memory of Dr. D. C. Sircar*, edited by Gouriswar Bhattacharya. Sri Satguru Publications, 1986.

Come here, O Jambhani, [you who] possess power, nourishers, [... Vajrī, as you are supreme and as you [... that Vajrapāṇi’s fair-faced one [... for the sake of sentient beings [... I shall speak, just as [... established by him of true promise [... a ray of light was emitted from the mark of a Great Man [... the illumination of the ray appeared. And by that ray [... they set out toward the Buddha-fields in the Sahā world.

(6) Bailey, Harold W. *Khotanese Buddhist Texts*. Cambridge Oriental Series 3. London: Taylor’s Foreign Press, 1951, pp. 135 ff. [Dhāraṇīs only] (i) *tadyathā vajradadi uku muku ukumapiṇi baddhani balacamara bāhuli bāhuli na hu hu huli vartaya svāhā* ||

(ii) Namely: Vajri, vajre, vajradhari, vajravati, vajradadi, vajra, vajre, vajredhare, paridhiri, bhiri bhiri, mure, cire, huhuri, bhaga, bhiri bhi, siririśi, cucura, u uci, bhiri, viri, cale, curi, muri, care, maṇḍa, nimaṇḍani! For the purpose of destroying all evil, for the pacification of all diseases, for the prevention of untimely death, and so on, up to the prevention of bad dreams, svāhā!
(iii) Namely: Maṇḍani, Gagaraṇi, Mūḍhane, Saṃpramūḍhani, Nāśani, Saṃpraṇāśani, Sarvavyādhipraśamani, and so on, up to Duḥsvaptākālamṛtyupratiṣedhani.

Namely: *nāśani nāśani baddhani baddhani bhindani chindani care mire sare hane vare vāre bare bare bhidi niribhidi bhiri bhiri rūṣpare śaraṇe vara varuṇe vara kāraṇḍaye brahmacāriṇe indravati dhidhirāyaṇi namo maheśvaralayani ṛṣibhājane pajahene (variant: pāpajahani) kālavādini (variant: °pātani) bhūtavādini (variant: ditto) satyakathe somavate somaprabhe svāhā.*
(v) Namely: *hara hara haraṇīye svāhā*.

(vi) Namely: *gaḍita*, *paḍita*, *ayena*, *ayajambahne*, *bakakardane*, *atraḍhahani*, *mārgābhirohaṇe*, *hūsavate*, *hūsavate*, *phusavate*, *pusavati*, *hili*, *heli*, *yathāvajri*, *yathāgni*, *yathāparaṃ ca*, *yathābhayaṃ*, *yathāparaṃ ca*, *yathāvajraṃ*, *yathāhṛdayam*.

(vii) Namely: *śikhi śikhi śikhaśe cici cici bhabha bhabha ruru ruru jiji jiji gragra gragra hrīhrī hrīhrī haha haha mama mama hana hana me sarvapratyarthikān daha daha me sarvaśatrūn paca paca me sarvāhiteṣiṇaḥ svāhā*.
(viii) Namely: *hili hili meli cili svāhā*, *brahmapure svāhā*, *brahmasvare svāhā*, *brahmābhe agarbhe puṣpe puṣpasaṃstare svāhā*.
(ix) Namely: *Vini cārṇe buddhamārtaṇḍe hana vi kha kha kha kha gorigāddhāri saramahāna vajrabharuṇi jvālamūlini vajravākeśadire śumare paramalate hana madyatāraṇi śāmbari svāhā*.
(x) Namely: Supuṣpe, Supuṣpe, Dhumaparihāre, Āryapraśaste, Śānte, Nirmukte, Maṅgalye, Hiraṇyagarbhe, Stūte, Stavite, Svāhā!
(xi) Namely: seli sespema seli sisseli pili mahāpippili simi lise gurūṇe gurūṇe mahāgurūṇe phu svāhā.
(xii) Namely: *aṭe phu vaṭe phu naṭe phu kunaṭe phu manaṭe phu muṇḍa hate phu śire phu bhaṅge phu macale phu svāhā*.
(xiii) Namely: Vajre vajre hrī vajre hrī vajre hī hī hī hī visi vise visi mahāvasi phu svāhā.
(xiv) Namely: *hulu hulu hulu lulu lulu lu lu lu sarvabhūtapratiṣedhanaṃ karomi svāhā*.
(xv) Namely: *Hili heli hili hilo halele lili hili hili, I perform the warding off of all spirits, svāhā!*
(xvi) Namely: *abge vaṅge caṅge hini didi didi cici phu svāhā | I perform the warding off of all spirits, svāhā!*
(xvii) Namely: *hate vihate nihate suhate sarvapratyarthikāḥ pratyamitrāḥ śuddhe mukte vimale nirmale prabhāsvare prabhāskare phu prabhākare phu svāhā*.
(xviii) Namely: *jvale jvale mahājvale jvale jvalini mahājvalini uke muke śame praśame mahāpraśame śame samādhe mahāsamādhe samāpte mahāsamāpte jvale mahājvale jvala bame phu svāhā*.

(xix) Namely: *udumbara udumbare pradumbara vyāvarte anaye samādhe mahāsamādhe samāpte mahāsamāpte nīle nīle nīlakule siddhe siddhamanorathe aṭe vaṭe naṭe kunaṭe samate bala kuce dāte dātte nīle nīle nīlakeśe kule mahākule nīlakānte jāṅgule huśe muhuśe vala jāṅgule phala kuce phala muce phu svāhā*.
(xx) Namely: Amale vimale nirmale maṅgalye hiraṇyagarbhe sarvārthasādhane mākaściniyukte viraje kaṭe keṭu keṭu kambale brahme brahmapure brahmasvare brahmasiddhe siddhamanorathe phu svāhā.

(xxi) Namely: *vajre vajre mahāvajre vajrapati buddhavajre buddhādhiṣṭhitavajre u buddhe nibuddhe saṃbuddhe bahubuddhe viśiṣṭe buddhe [viśiṣṭabuddhe] buddhe buddhe buddhe deśaṃgāmenika jaṅgame amale tamale tili tile tilele mārge mārgātagāmane phu svāhā*.

(xxii) Namely: *hihi vajre hihi vajre hehe vajre*, and so on, up to *kiri kiri vajra svāhā*. Namely: *aṇḍare paṇḍare śvete pāṇḍaravāsini kinnare karāḍe keyūre iha buddhe tatra buddhe bhūje bhūje bhūje bhujagapate bhaye bhaye bhayāgre bhayāgrapate vini vini śiri śiripati śīmapati ādityapati teje tejapati ākārapate phu svāhā*.

(xxiii) Namely: *kuṭe kuṭe kuṭa kuṭa kuṭani kuṭa kuṭare svāhā | nīle nīle nīlakeśe svāhā pīte pīte pītakeśe svāhā lohite lohite lohitakeśe svāhā avadāte avadāte avadātakeśe svāhā mañjiṣṭhe mañjiṣṭhe mañjiṣṭhakeśe svāhā cakre cakre cakrā cakre vajracakre svāhā*.
